extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership and staff, IT/OCIO teams, patent and trademark practitioners, policy makers, and external stakeholders interested in USPTO operational standards
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the USPTO's FY2021 operational objectives, technical standards, program requirements, and policy criteria covering cybersecurity, IT modernization, data/open-data practices, analytics/AI/ML, RPA, fee-setting, acquisition, and practitioner admission/representation rules. Useful for people implementing or evaluating USPTO processes and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous and automated security across software lifecycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous and automated security at the early stages of software development and throughout the product life cycle with measures to ensure supply chain risk management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement emerging security technology, security architecture, security operations best practices, and an improved risk management framework; foster a cyclical practice of identifying, prioritizing, and remediating known vulnerabilities and weaknesses—with high-value assets as a priority—through continuous monitoring and maintaining a standard policy on time to remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize remediation for high-value assets and time-to-remediation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Foster a cyclical practice of identifying, prioritizing, and remediating known vulnerabilities and weaknesses—with its high-value assets as a priority—through monitoring continuously and maintaining a standard policy on time to remediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms) and reduce open POA&Ms; measure progress (FY2021 saw a 60% decrease in open POA&Ms across products through improved remediation efforts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition from end-of-support platforms to secure versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on the transition of products from end-of-support platforms to the latest, secure versions to improve security posture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work to replace unsupported/authentication systems (e.g., permanently turn off previously unsupported authentication) and update legacy systems to vendor-supported hardware/software to reduce vulnerabilities and technical debt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with EO 14028 and zero-trust architecture
rubrics_metrics.description: Align IT and security modernization efforts with Executive Order 14028 on Improving the Nation’s Cybersecurity and adopt mandated zero-trust security model architecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver network and system architectures that comply with EO 14028; the Chief Architect delivered archetypes for complete pipeline delivery to AWS aligned with a zero-trust model.

rubrics_metrics.name: FedRAMP-compliant public cloud services
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish additional enterprise services in the public cloud that are compliant with the Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cloud product teams should deploy products to public cloud providers that meet FedRAMP compliance; example: establishing FedRAMP-compliant connections for AWS and Google.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPA governance and Center of Excellence standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish an enterprise capability and Center of Excellence (CoE) for Robotic Process Automation (RPA) that supports federated development and communicates RPA information and practices across the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralize RPA infrastructure and licensing to promote standardization, technology congruence, governance, software reuse, and bulk purchasing. CoE should establish guidelines to standardize repeatable processes, feed automated test and deployment pipelines, and promote agile and DevSecOps aligned with the NWOW product catalog.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPA deployment and measurable automation savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Deploy RPA bots to automate tedious tasks with measurable time savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track deployments and time savings (examples: 13 bots deployed; specific bots saved 108, 256, and 3,081 hours per year in cited functions). Forecast increased bot adoption as savings accrue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open data definition and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Open data is publicly available data that is structured to be fully discoverable and usable by end users and can be freely used, reused, and redistributed by anyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in enhancing open data efforts (Developer Hub/Open Data Portal) to promote equitable opportunities and fuel innovation, research, and commercial activity; participate in and enable datasets for AI research (e.g., contribution to the Pile Dataset).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Examination Data System (PEDS) image and metadata repository
rubrics_metrics.description: Deploy a new cloud-based repository of the image file wrapper and metadata for nearly 10 million applications previously accessible in Public PAIR, and make these images and data available to users via APIs and bulk download services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose images through a new 'tab' in PEDS and expand API/bulk download accessibility in the near future to support external users and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern analytics infrastructure migration and consolidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Migrate the centralized analytical platform to support a multicloud, hybrid infrastructure; consolidate data analytics components; implement data cataloging and model management technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide on-demand flexibility for business units to stand up project-specific analytical data stores and models; centralize enterprise management of role authentication, access controls, data governance, and provisioning; make accurate, timely algorithms/models and reporting accessible to authorized stakeholders to reduce replication and support analytics/AI/ML work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate data silos through cultural and organizational change
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-IT initiatives must focus on organizational cultural changes to support shared data management and governance practices so that data collections held by one group are accessible to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maturing integrations and shared governance will reduce duplicated development effort, time spent preparing data, and will fuel innovation driven by centralized data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalize AI/ML with strong OCIO-business partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Operationalizing ML and AI requires a strong partnership between OCIO and its internal customers and aligns with the shift to a product-based model and strategic IT themes (advanced analytics, AI, ML, automation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop, deliver, and manage AI/ML tools to improve processing, increase quality and efficiency, and support decision-making; example: USPTO received recognition (FutureEdge50) for these efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: DevSecOps, Agile Delivery, and code/reuse platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish an Agile Delivery Platform to increase DevSecOps velocity toward deployments, ease secure cloud adoption through automated testing and configuration management, and facilitate code sharing and reuse across product teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform accelerates onboarding, supports AWS cloud pipelines, and enables standardized deployment practices; Identity-as-a-Service (Okta) adoption to replace legacy RBAC supports consistent security controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: eCommerce modernization and DOCX/smart XML submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a cohesive login system (Single Sign On) and receive smart text XML versions of key patent application documents (e.g., DOCX) to increase automation in processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use DOCX to accept text-based applications, file drawings in DOCX, support Hague design applications, enable third-party submissions; create beta-test groups and training (USPTO trained over 11,000 users) to refine submission processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent examiner tools modernization and data migration
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve examiner tools (DAV, DM, Official Correspondence, new examiner search tool) and migrate large collections (70+ million image/text files with English translations) to support examination performance and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make DM performance info available to examiners, add troubleshooting tools, scale search tool correctness and performance, train examiners (2,500 trained in FY2021 with more to follow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee-setting principles and maintaining operating reserves
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO fees must balance fee income, costs, organizational risks, and public policy objectives; maintain operating reserves to mitigate uncertain demand and ensure financial stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee schedules consider service delivery costs and policy objectives (e.g., discounts for small businesses and micro-entities); use sophisticated planning and budgeting models; engage public dialogue for preliminary fee proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark fee rule objectives and response to filing surges
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust trademark fees to finance the full cost of the trademark business, protect the integrity of the Trademark Register, and improve the efficiency of agency processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use additional revenue to add examining attorneys, support staff, contractors, and IT solutions to reduce backlogs and process applications faster and more effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition strategy: re-competition and multi-vendor contracting
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-compete large sole-source contracts into competitive, multi-vendor contracts with service and cost incentives to save money and reduce operational risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New contracts should enable cost savings (example: projected $150 million savings over 10 years), improve contingency planning, increase physical and cybersecurity requirements, include subcontracting plans supporting small businesses, and incorporate backup locations for continuity and climate resiliency.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Requirements Bulletin (GRB) criteria for patent registration exam
rubrics_metrics.description: Three categories of technical and scientific qualifications may make applicants eligible: Category A (specified bachelor’s degrees), Category B (other bachelor’s degrees with technical/scientific training), and Category C (practical engineering or scientific experience); independent review if applicant does not qualify under categories per CFR § 11.7(a)(2)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on public comments and evaluation, changes were made: add common Category B degrees to Category A; accept advanced degrees (master’s, Ph.D.) under Category A; accept combination of core sciences under Category B (Options 2 and 4) if one core science course has a lab component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation rules update (37 CFR part 11) and signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise part 11 to align USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct more closely with ABA Model Rules, revise deadlines/procedures related to registration exam/reinstatement/limited recognition, and make non-substantive comprehensibility improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published final rule eliminated the requirement for original, handwritten signatures in correspondence related to registration to practice, enrollment and disciplinary matters, and certain credit-card payments not made via USPTO electronic filing systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure product team KPIs and cost-efficiency measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Product teams should increase resiliency/redundancy, maximize compute power, and achieve cost efficiencies through cloud strategy, data center relocations, server decommission automation, storage reclamation, and migration to open-source software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: optimized monthly cloud costs (35% AWS reduction), reduced 567 TB storage (annual cost avoidance $755,300), NetBackup migration savings ($2.6M), projected $600,000 reduction in license costs from open-source migration.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-user support and continuity of operations practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide enhanced customer value via proactive 2FA replacements, software license asset deployments and training, adoption of collaboration tools (Microsoft Teams), and maintaining up-to-date contact center solution databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively replace expiring authentication tokens for users unable to update; deploy license management to ensure cost savings and MEGABYTE Act compliance; host enterprise engagement events (Team Stream) and maintain accurate solutions databases for timely public responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emerging technology prototyping and evaluation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide exploratory support for prototypes and proofs of concept (e.g., blockchain for electronic trademark certificates, chatbot for 24/7 basic queries, elastic search solutions, large-file upload/processing, Secure Access Service Edge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate multiple technical solutions (six solutions evaluated for large-file processing); adopt those that increase public satisfaction, reduce costs, improve cybersecurity posture and enable new capabilities (e.g., accept larger file attachments such as bio-sequence data files).
